# **The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle**

The **Asian Giant Softshell Turtle** (*Pelochelys cantorii*) is one of the world’s largest freshwater turtles, native to Southeast Asia. Weighing up to **250 pounds (113 kg)** and measuring over **3 feet (1 m)** in length, this rare species inhabits rivers, lakes, and estuaries in countries like **Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, and Malaysia** (WWF). Unlike most turtles, it has a **soft, leathery shell** instead of a hard one, allowing it to swim swiftly.

This turtle is **carnivorous**, feeding on fish, crustaceans, and even small vertebrates. It is known for its **ambush hunting technique**, burying itself in sand or mud and striking prey with its powerful jaws (Turtle Conservancy). Tragically, the species is **Critically Endangered** due to **habitat destruction, pollution, and hunting** for its meat and eggs (IUCN Red List). Conservation efforts, such as captive breeding programs in Cambodia, aim to prevent its extinction.

Efforts to protect this species include **community education, habitat restoration, and anti-poaching laws**. Wildlife organizations like the **WWF and Turtle Conservancy** work to raise awareness about its ecological importance, as it helps maintain balanced aquatic ecosystems.

![Asian Giant Softshell Turtle in water](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Pelochelys_cantorii_01.jpg/800px-Pelochelys_cantorii_01.jpg)
*An Asian Giant Softshell Turtle in its natural habitat.*

![Close-up of the turtle's head](https://www.turtlesurvival.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/Pelochelys-cantorii-Asian-Giant-Softshell-Turtle.jpg)
*A close-up of the turtle’s distinctive snout and eyes.*

- "Asian Giant Softshell Turtle." *World Wildlife Fund*, WWF, [www.worldwildlife.org](https://www.worldwildlife.org).
- "Pelochelys cantorii – Asian Giant Softshell Turtle." *Turtle Conservancy*, 2021, [turtleconservancy.org](https://turtleconservancy.org).
